title: Stabilize egress path selection to prevent tenant DNS response reassociation
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Several Dedicated customers observed intermittent DNS responses being attributed to the wrong tenant after a pool failover or peering reconfiguration. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and the permanent fix to make egress path selection deterministic and tenant-safe across peering/scale events.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision two tenant VPCs A and B with peering through dedicated egress pools.
Trigger a rolling restart of the dedicated egress pool (simulate autoscaler-driven reparenting).
Generate outbound DNS queries from both tenants under load (200 qps each) and capture resolver responses and SNAT mappings at the egress nodes.
Observe intermittent correlation where DNS responses appear to come from the ephemeral SNAT mapping of the other tenant after the pool swap.
customer_reports: HC-Enterprise: production search service intermittently returned private hostnames from another tenant; SRE noticed resolver mapping changes immediately after an egress pool failover (support ticket #64211).

ScaleApps: reported recurring 503s for internal APIs and traced to mismatched egress metadata where our resolver returned cached records from an unrelated tenant during peering update (support ticket #64720).
Two additional customers provided packet captures showing DNS response source IP swap within seconds of BGP/peering state change.
mitigation: Immediate: rate-limit peering reconvergence events per tenant to avoid concurrent reparenting across many dedicated pools (rolled out as a control-plane throttle on 2026-03-02).
Short-term: invalidate per-tenant resolver cache entries on any egress-path change for 30s (feature flag enabled in prod 2026-03-03).
Workaround for customers: recommend setting dedicated egress affinity to 'sticky' for critical routes until permanent fix is deployed.
root_cause_summary: Race between egress reparenting logic and SNAT table reclamation allowed ephemeral SNAT entries to be reused across tenants in a small time window. Concurrent peering flaps and control-plane reconcilers updated route bindings without coordinating SNAT and per-tenant resolver cache invalidation, enabling DNS responses to be served from wrong tenant context.
implementation_notes: Add deterministic egress path token (egress-hash + tenant-id) propagated into SNAT allocation to prevent reuse across tenants until mapping is fully released.

Introduce control-plane barrier during peering reconfiguration that sequences: drain traffic -> freeze SNAT reuse -> update route bindings -> release SNATs -> unfreeze. This ensures no overlapping ownership windows.
Extend resolver cache key to include egress-path-token so stale cache cannot be hit after reparenting.
Update kernel/iptables SNAT allocation shim to track tenant-id labels and refuse reuse within 60s of release when peering state changed.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy egress-path-token propagation and cache-key change to 5% of dedicated pools in us-west on 2026-03-08; monitor DNS misassociation metric and per-tenant DNS error rate.
Stage 2 (ramp): expand to 50% after 48h of stable canary results; enable SNAT reuse guard on remaining pools in same window.
Stage 3 (global): full rollout across regions and dedicated pools with coordinated control-plane barrier enforcement; schedule during low-traffic windows and customer-notified maintenance
qa_checklist: Unit tests: egress-token generation and propagation across route bind and SNAT shim.
Integration tests: simulate concurrent peering reconfig with high qps to ensure no cross-tenant SNAT reuse.
Chaos test: introduce random pool restarts and BGP flaps; assert DNS cache isolation and no cross-tenant responses for 1000 simulated tenants.
Performance test: verify no >5% regression in p95 latency for DNS under typical load after new token added.
